definition: Classifying affect, arousal, and other speaker states from how something is said rather than what is said, part of the broader paralinguistics family (speaker traits, health signals).
details: Classifying affect, arousal, and other speaker states from how something is said rather than what is said, part of the broader paralinguistics family (speaker traits, health signals). Increasingly folded into speech LLMs that describe emotion and speaking style in natural language.

explainer.lead: Classifying affect, arousal, and other speaker states from how something is said rather than what is said. It belongs to the broader paralinguistics family covering speaker traits and health signals.

tiers.eli5: It is about hearing that someone sounds upset or excited, regardless of the words they use.
tiers.practitioner: Systems increasingly handle this inside speech LLMs that describe emotion and speaking style in natural language rather than emitting only a label. A pitfall is that the signal lives in delivery, not transcripts, so text-only pipelines lose it.
tiers.paperLevel: Speech emotion recognition classifies affect, arousal, and other speaker states from vocal delivery; it is part of the paralinguistics family alongside speaker traits and health signals. Limit: it targets speaker state rather than lexical content.

explainer.example: A speech LLM listens to a customer's utterance and outputs that the speaker sounds hesitant and frustrated.
